newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria extends terms for sale of chemical plant.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria extends terms for sale of chemical plant.

text.p: Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said on Thursday it had extended the term for negotiations for the sale of a 57 percent stake in the country's chemical fertiliser producer Chimko.

"After the second round of negotiations with the potential buyers of Chimko AD in the town of Vratsa, the Privatisation Agency fixes a new term for updating the offers which is September 12," said an agency statement, faxed to Reuters.
The agency expects the bidders to improve their offers and that is why it gives them time for it, an agency official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
The agency opened a new round for Chimko's partial sale in May, setting a minimum price of $100.2 million for the stake after South Korea's Daewoo previous bid was deemed too low.
Daewoo, which set up a local subsidiary in Bulgaria in 1992, is also one of the bidders for Chimko in the second round.
Chimko has 20 installations, including for reforming, carbamide, carbon sulphide, carbon dioxide and a catalytic installation.
The plant imports 64 percent of its raw materials and exports 92 percent of its products.
The Vratsa-based plant sees its annual net profit for this year at some $20 million.
